clusters.name: Your stepfather Desmond settling into the family, 1987
clusters.reason: Around 1987, when you began secondary school, three shifts pile up: you and Desmond grew more distant, you leaned harder toward your dad for notice, and your stepparents separated over starting a family; that autumn you made the chess squad and your anxiety rose. These are your shifts and your father's family's, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death and your move to secondary school, 1989–1992
clusters.reason: From 1989 to early 1992, shifts pile up around your grandfather's return to the family, your move to the rebuilt house with Desmond's children, and his death in 1991. Within those years: your late nights and sleep troubles began and stayed, you dropped chess and debate, you underfunctioned on college forms while your mother filled them in, you fused with Rafe at conservatory, a wrist injury stopped your playing and your anxiety and functioning fell, you and Rafe had a blow-up, you got high and absorbed yourself in radios, and by early 1992 you were lost and low with no footing. Your grandmother was treated for thyroid cancer around the same time. The period reaches from your grandfather's return in early 1989 to the spring of 1992, when you earned money fixing radios and things began to settle.

clusters.name: Your burnout from performing and the end of your relationship with Marisol, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: From 2001 to early 2004, around your grandmother's cancer diagnosis and your disastrous audition, shifts pile up month by month: you ran out of steam for performing, your anxiety rose and functioning fell, you grew distant from your parents, you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, you met Marisol and moved to Fenwick, you split within the year, you sank into deep depression and could not face your family, you relied on friends instead, your dad and Corbin talked together, and you began swimming and returned to your therapist. Your grandmother died in February 2004 near the end. The period settles as you began to recover through therapy and moved toward your parents again.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and the cutoff from your mother, 2008
clusters.reason: Around early 2008, when your grandmother died and you went to nursing school, shifts pile up in a few months: your grandmother and grandfather died, you spent weeks building at Alder Creek and grew too drained to talk with your mother, she pressed to visit and you kept the door shut, and you stopped speaking to her when you moved to Marlow Sound. The silence held for roughly a year. No one else's shifts show in these months.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and her mother's retirement, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: From your wedding in March 2017 through late October 2019, shifts pile up around your marriage, Wren's close ties with her father and brother, and her mother's retirement party: you and your mother grew slightly more distant, your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, Tara married and had a baby on the way, Wren's aunt began showing memory loss and lashing out, your job steadied and your anxiety eased, but by autumn 2019 your anxiety rose again as you felt you ought to push your projects forward, you started a sleeping pill, you aimed for shorter regular calls with your mother, Wren became swamped with events, you overfunctioned laying out a plan for her, her family fused around her needs, and at the lake house weekend your sleep broke and you felt you did not belong. The period reaches from the spring of 2017 through late October 2019, settling as things quieted after the weekend.
